{{Recipe}}

The following recipe, taken from ''The Cook's Decameron: A Study In Taste'', apparently dates from the late 19th century.<ref>{{cite book |last=Waters |first=Mrs. W.G. |title=The Cook's Decameron: A Study In Taste |date=1920 |publisher=IndyPublish.com |isbn=1404345809}}</ref> It bears no relation whatsoever to the classic [[Cookbook:Espagnole Sauce|espagnole]], as it is not thickened except for a tiny amount of flour and should only be regarded as a curiosity.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] (55 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* Slices of [[Cookbook:Veal|veal]], [[Cookbook:Ham|ham]], [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon]], [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]], or [[Cookbook:Poultry|poultry]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Peppercorn|peppercorns]]
* [[Cookbook:Mushroom|Mushroom]] trimmings
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomato]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]] [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], studded with 2 [[Cookbook:Clove|cloves]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]] [[Cookbook:Turnip|turnip]]
* 1 sprig each of [[Cookbook:Thyme|thyme]], [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]], and [[Cookbook:Marjoram|marjoram]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Pint|pint]] (150 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Stock|stock]]

== Procedure ==
# Grease the bottom of a stew pan with butter.
# Add the meat, peppercorns, mushroom trimmings, tomato, carrot, turnip cut up, onion, bay leaf, thyme, parsley, and marjoram. [[Cookbook:Braising|Braise]] well for 15 minutes with the lid on.
# Add the stock and [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] gently for 15 minutes.
# Strain through a [[Cookbook:Tamis|tamis]], then remove excess grease.
# Cool in an earthenware vessel, and add glaze if desired.
# Pass through a [[Cookbook:Sieve|sieve]] before serving.
